Dr. '''Alan Gelperin''' is a [[scientist]] and [[biologist]] currently at [[Princeton University]]. He is an emeritus faculty member at [[Monell Chemical Senses Center]]. He specializes in [[Electronic nose|electronic olfaction]] and [[computational neuroscience]]. He received his bachelor's degree in biology from [[Carleton College]] in 1962 and went on to get a Ph.D. from University of Pennsylvania.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://apps.carleton.edu/alumni/directory/?full_names=alan+gelperin|title=alan gelperin {{!}} Alumni Directory {{!}} Carleton College|website=apps.carleton.edu|language=en-US|access-date=2018-08-18}}</ref>

He is most notable for his efforts in creating robots with electronic noses which can localize odors, and for the invention of a [[supermarket]] fruit and vegetable scanner that does not use barcodes but instead scans by scent.<ref>{{Citation
